title: Cohorted Fallback & Progression Framework for Model Degradation Experiments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an experiment orchestration pattern that allows us to run controlled model-degradation tests for latency-sensitive routes. The framework will create small, cohorted traffic slices that exercise fallback and progressive routing rules when a primary model experiences quality or latency regressions. Goals: (1) standardize milestone definitions and gating thresholds across A/B tests and canaries, (2) provide a reusable progression plan (0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50%) with automated rollback triggers, and (3) surface clear diagnostics for root-cause decisions (model variant, quantization level, infra region). This ticket captures the PM-side playbook, acceptance criteria, and required observability hooks for implementation by ENG and Design. The output should be a checklist + templated stages that SREs, Product, and Solutions Eng can re-use for next 12 months of experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Template with four progression stages (initial, ramp-1, ramp-2, wide) defined and documented
Automated gating matrix wired to metrics and rollbacks (latency p95, error rate, quality regression score)
Runbook and owner assignments for each stage included in the ticket
Experiment template stored in Confluence and linked from Console experiment create flow
Two end-to-end dry-run experiments executed (internal traffic) and results documented
milestones: Milestone 1 - Draft playbook & gating matrix (2026-02-27): baseline metrics and candidate thresholds
Milestone 2 - Observability hooks and dashboard spec (2026-03-06): query templates, alerts, and segmentation
Milestone 3 - Template integration & SRE signoff (2026-03-20): experiment create flow stub
Milestone 4 - Dry-run execution + lessons learned (2026-03-31): two internal cohorts run
Milestone 5 - Public rollout and docs release (2026-04-15): publish Confluence template and update Console help
metrics: Cost: tokens-per-request and GPU-ops estimate change
Quality: weighted automated eval score (prompt-suite) and human sample checks
Error rate: total request failures and model-side decoding errors
Fallback rate: percent of requests requiring fallback variant or cached reply
gating_rules: Fail-fast: if latency p95 increases by >50% vs baseline for 5m window -> immediate rollback to previous stage
Quality sentinel: if automated eval score drops >3 points on primary prompt-suite over any 1,000-sample window -> pause and notify
Progress rule: advance only after 24h at current stage with stable metrics and no alerts
Manual override: CRO/PM/SRE approval required to continue if any customer-impacting signal is present
monitoring: Console dashboard: experiment overview with cohort sizes, routing policy, and top three anomalous signals
Alerting: PagerDuty for P0 regressions (latency and error spikes), Slack channel for experiment chatter
Sampling hooks: automated 1-in-500 human annotation sample for quality regression verification
Trace links: link to distributed traces and request-level logs for affected cohorts
